name: Viktor Korchnoi
milestone_by_age_26: Awarded the Grandmaster title by FIDE in 1956 at age 25, after winning international tournaments in Bucharest (1954) and Hastings (1955-56) and finishing 2nd-3rd in the USSR Championship.
early_history_summary: Korchnoi learned chess at age five from his father and joined the Leningrad Pioneer Palace chess club in 1943. He won the USSR Junior Championship in 1947 at age 16, earned the Soviet Master title in 1951, and qualified for the USSR Championship finals starting in 1952. His first international tournament victory came at Bucharest 1954, leading to the International Master title that year and the Grandmaster title in 1956.
family_context_summary: Born to a Jewish pianist mother and Polish-Catholic engineer father in Leningrad; parents divorced early and his father was killed during the siege of Leningrad in 1941. His stepmother raised him thereafter.
parent_family_domain_summary: His mother was a pianist and alumna of the Leningrad Conservatory; his father was an engineer. No documented family background in chess beyond his father teaching him the game at age five.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Soviet chess pipeline,Pioneer Palace training,elite coaching,war hardship
evidence_summary: Korchnoi benefited from the Soviet chess development pipeline, joining the Leningrad Pioneer Palace chess club at age 12 and receiving training from Abram Model and Vladimir Zak, who had previously trained world champions Botvinnik and Spassky. He won the USSR Junior Championship at 16 and earned the Grandmaster title by 25, embedded in the world's strongest national chess system. The siege of Leningrad created severe early hardship, though no evidence of family financial advantage was found.

name: Sándor Kocsis
milestone_by_age_26: Won Olympic gold at the 1952 Helsinki Olympics with Hungary and was the top goalscorer in any European league in 1952 with 36 goals for Honvéd, all before age 26.
early_history_summary: Kocsis began his career as a junior with Kőbányai TC before joining Ferencváros in 1946 at age 17, where he won his first Hungarian League title in 1949. He was conscripted into the army and joined Honvéd, where he became the league's top goalscorer in 1951 (30 goals), 1952 (36 goals), and 1954 (33 goals), and won multiple league titles. He made his Hungary national team debut in 1948 and scored six goals at the 1952 Olympics.
family_context_summary: Born in Budapest; no documented family background in football or details of financial status found in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Hungarian football golden era,Honvéd army club,Puskás teammates,early professional debut
evidence_summary: Kocsis emerged from the Hungarian football system at a time when it was the world's strongest, joining Ferencváros at 17 and winning a league title at 20. At Honvéd he played alongside Puskás, Czibor, and Bozsik in the Golden Team era, becoming Europe's top league goalscorer at 23 and winning Olympic gold the same year. No family background information was found in reviewed sources, but the concentration of elite talent at Honvéd and in the national team provided a powerful peer ecosystem.

name: Jerzy Grotowski
milestone_by_age_26: Founded and became artistic director of the Theatre of 13 Rows in Opole in 1959 at age 26, after making his directorial debut in 1958, establishing the company that would become the internationally influential Laboratory Theatre.
early_history_summary: Grotowski studied acting and directing at the Ludwik Solski Academy of Dramatic Arts in Kraków and the Russian Academy of Theatre Arts in Moscow. He made his directorial debut in 1957-58 in Kraków and was invited by theatre critic Ludwik Flaszen to take over as artistic director of the Theatre of 13 Rows in Opole in 1959, where he assembled a company of young actors and began developing his experimental methods.
family_context_summary: Born in Rzeszów, southeastern Poland; during World War II he moved with his mother and brother to the village of Nienadówka. No documented family financial status or domain background found.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Kraków drama academy,Moscow theatre training,Flaszen collaboration,postwar Polish theatre
evidence_summary: Grotowski trained at two elite dramatic arts institutions (Kraków and Moscow), giving him unusual depth in theatrical method at a young age. At 26 he took over the Theatre of 13 Rows in Opole with critic Ludwik Flaszen, assembling a company of young Kraków graduates. His wartime childhood and postwar Polish context shaped his experimental approach. No family domain background was documented in reviewed sources.

name: Flavio Briatore
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Briatore worked as a ski instructor, restaurant manager, and assistant to a businessman before meeting Luciano Benetton; his career breakthrough came at age 29 when Benetton appointed him to lead US operations in 1979.
early_history_summary: Briatore failed public school twice, attended a private school, and received a diploma in land surveying with the lowest grades. He worked as a ski instructor and restaurant manager, opened an unsuccessful restaurant, and became an assistant to businessman Attilio Dutto before moving to Milan to work at the Italian stock exchange, where he met Luciano Benetton.
family_context_summary: Born in Verzuolo near Cuneo in the Maritime Alps; parents were school teachers. No documented family business background.
evidence_summary: Briatore's early career was characterized by failed ventures and odd jobs with no material business milestone by age 26. His parents were school teachers with no documented business platform. His breakthrough came at 29 through the Benetton connection.

name: Toshiro Mifune
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Mifune served in the Imperial Japanese Army from 1940 to 1945; his acting career began at age 27 in 1947 when he entered Toho's 'new faces' contest, with his breakthrough coming in Rashomon (1950) at age 30.
early_history_summary: Mifune grew up in Dalian, China, and worked at his father's photo studio. He was drafted into the Imperial Japanese Army Aviation division in 1940 and served in the Aerial Photography unit through World War II until 1945. After the war, he applied to Toho Studios' 'new faces' contest in 1947 at age 27, which launched his acting career.
family_context_summary: Born in Qingdao, China, to Japanese parents; his father was a trade merchant and photographer who ran a photography business, and his mother was the daughter of a hatamoto (high-ranking samurai official). Parents were Methodist missionaries.
evidence_summary: Mifune's acting career did not begin until age 27 due to military service from ages 20-25. No material acting milestone occurred by age 26. His father's photography business provided early exposure to visual media but no direct acting domain advantage was documented.

name: Klaus Kinski
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Kinski had small theater roles and bit film parts (first film Morituri, 1948) but was fired from the Schlosspark-Theater in 1947 and had no notable breakthrough; his international recognition came with Werner Herzog films starting in 1972 at age 46.
early_history_summary: Kinski was conscripted into the Wehrmacht in 1943 at age 17, captured by the British in 1944, and began acting in POW camp variety shows. After returning to Germany in 1946, he was hired by the Schlosspark-Theater in Berlin but fired in 1947 for unpredictable behavior. He had a small film role in 1948 and worked as a touring monologist, but gained no material recognition by age 26.
family_context_summary: Born in Zoppot, Free City of Danzig; his father was an opera singer who became a pharmacist, and his mother was a nurse and daughter of a pastor. The family moved to Berlin in 1931 and experienced financial difficulties. Herzog claimed Kinski was actually raised upper middle class.
evidence_summary: Kinski's early career was marked by instability and small roles with no material milestone by age 26. His wartime experiences and POW camp theater provided his first acting exposure, but he was fired from his first professional theater job and had only bit film parts before 26.

name: Denzel Washington
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Washington had a TV movie debut in 1977 and was doing theater work, but his career breakthrough came with St. Elsewhere (1982) at age 28 and his first Oscar for Glory (1989) at age 35.
early_history_summary: Washington graduated from Fordham University in 1977 with a BA in Drama and Journalism, attended the American Conservatory Theater for one year, and made his screen debut in the 1977 TV film Wilma. He performed in off-Broadway theater and summer stock but had no major film or television role by age 26. His first Hollywood film (Carbon Copy) came in 1981 at age 27.
family_context_summary: Born in Mount Vernon, New York; mother was a beauty parlor owner and operator, father was an ordained Pentecostal minister and NYC Water Department employee. Parents divorced when he was 14, and he was sent to a private military academy.
evidence_summary: Washington's acting career was in its earliest stages by age 26, with only a TV movie debut and theater work. His formal training at Fordham and the American Conservatory Theater provided a foundation, but no material milestone occurred before 26.

name: Roger Glover
milestone_by_age_26: Joined Deep Purple in 1969 at age 24 and by age 26 had recorded the landmark albums Deep Purple in Rock (1970) and Fireball (1971) as bassist of one of the world's biggest hard rock bands.
early_history_summary: Glover began playing guitar at age 13 after moving to London, and formed his first band, the Madisons, at Harrow County School for Boys. The band merged with rivals to become Episode Six, which featured future Deep Purple bandmate Ian Gillan. After years of gigging and recording with Episode Six, Glover and Gillan joined Deep Purple in 1969, transforming the band's sound and launching their most successful era.
family_context_summary: Born near Brecon, Wales, and moved to South Kensington, London at age nine. No documented family musical background or financial details found in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: London rock scene,Episode Six reps,Ian Gillan partnership,hard rock wave
evidence_summary: Glover benefited from growing up in London during the 1960s rock explosion, forming Episode Six as a teenager and building years of gigging and songwriting experience with Ian Gillan before joining Deep Purple at 24. The complementary partnership with Gillan was central to the transition. No family musical background or financial advantage was documented in reviewed sources.

name: Keanu Reeves
milestone_by_age_26: Achieved his first major commercial success with Bill & Ted's Excellent Adventure (1989) at age 25, following critically acclaimed roles in River's Edge (1986) and Dangerous Liaisons (1988).
early_history_summary: Reeves began acting in Toronto at age 16, appearing in the CBC television series Hangin' In (1984). He made his feature film debut in Youngblood (1986), earned critical acclaim in River's Edge (1986), and appeared in Dangerous Liaisons (1988) before his breakthrough commercial success in Bill & Ted's Excellent Adventure (1989). He dropped out of high school at 17 and moved to Los Angeles with a green card through his American stepfather.
family_context_summary: Born in Beirut to an English costume designer mother and an American father of Hawaiian, Chinese, English, and Portuguese descent. Parents divorced in 1966; mother moved family to Sydney, then New York, then Toronto. Mother married Broadway/Hollywood director Paul Aaron in 1970, who gave Reeves career advice.
parent_family_domain_summary: Mother was a costume designer and performer; stepfather Paul Aaron was a Broadway and Hollywood director who offered career advice and recommended a job at the Hedgerow Theatre in Pennsylvania.
primary_early_advantage_tags: stepfather director connection,Toronto acting scene,early TV debut,dyslexia adversity
evidence_summary: Reeves had early exposure to the entertainment industry through his mother's work as a costume designer and his stepfather Paul Aaron's career as a Broadway and Hollywood director, who provided career guidance. He began acting at 16 in Toronto, moved to LA at 20, and achieved commercial breakthrough at 25 with Bill & Ted's. Dyslexia and family instability created early adversity but also urgency to pursue acting.

name: Dragan Džajić
milestone_by_age_26: Made his first-team debut for Red Star Belgrade at 17 and won his first Yugoslav league championship in 1964 at age 18, going on to win five league titles and four cups with Red Star and earning 85 caps for Yugoslavia by the end of his career.
early_history_summary: Džajić was spotted by Red Star Belgrade youth coach Miljan Miljanić at a junior tournament and joined the club's youth system at 15. He made his first-team debut at 17 years and 8 days in June 1963, won his first championship in 1964, and made his Yugoslavia national team debut at 18. By 26 he had won multiple league titles and was a key player for both club and country, including scoring the famous winning goal against England in the Euro 1968 semi-final.
family_context_summary: Born in the small town of Ub, 60 kilometers outside Belgrade. No documented family background in football or financial details found in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Red Star Belgrade youth system,Miljanić scouting,early first-team debut,Yugoslav football
evidence_summary: Džajić was scouted by Red Star Belgrade's youth coach Miljan Miljanić at 15 and fast-tracked to the first team at 17, benefiting from one of Eastern Europe's premier club academies. He won his first league title at 18 and became a national team regular by the same age. No family background information was documented in reviewed sources, but the Red Star pipeline provided elite training, facilities, and competitive exposure from a young age.

name: Charles K. Kao
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Kao had completed a B.Sc. from Woolwich Polytechnic in 1957 and started work at Standard Telecommunication Laboratories, but his groundbreaking fibre optics research was published in 1966 at age 33 and his PhD was awarded in 1965 at age 32.
early_history_summary: Kao moved from Shanghai to Hong Kong in 1949, graduated from St. Joseph's College in 1952, went to London for further study, and earned a B.Sc. from Woolwich Polytechnic in 1957. He then began doctoral research at University College London while working at Standard Telecommunication Laboratories, but his pioneering work on fibre optic communications did not emerge until 1966.
family_context_summary: Born in Shanghai; father was a judge and professor with a JD from University of Michigan Law School. Grandfather was a scholar, poet, and artist. Family settled in Hong Kong in 1949 after the Communist Revolution.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a law professor and judge with a US law degree; grandfather was a scholar, poet, and artist. Family had strong academic traditions but not in engineering or physics specifically.
evidence_summary: Kao's early career followed a standard academic path with a B.Sc. at 24 and entry-level engineering work, with no material milestone by 26. His family had strong academic traditions (father a law professor, grandfather a scholar) but no direct engineering domain advantage. His Nobel-winning fibre optics work came at age 33.

name: David J. Thouless
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Thouless completed his PhD at Cornell under Hans Bethe in 1958 at age 24 and was a postdoctoral researcher at Berkeley, but his groundbreaking contributions to topological phase transitions came in the 1970s; a PhD and postdoc are standard academic steps, not material independent milestones.
early_history_summary: Thouless was educated at Winchester College and Trinity Hall, Cambridge, earning a BA in Natural Sciences. He obtained his PhD at Cornell University under Hans Bethe in 1958 at age 24, then worked as a postdoctoral researcher at Lawrence Berkeley Laboratory. His first academic book was published in 1961 at age 27, and his major theoretical contributions emerged in the 1970s.
family_context_summary: Born in Bearsden, Scotland, to English parents; mother was an English teacher, father was Robert Thouless, a psychologist and broadcaster.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a psychologist and broadcaster; mother was an English teacher. No direct family background in physics was documented.
evidence_summary: Thouless followed a standard elite academic path through Winchester College, Cambridge, and a Cornell PhD under Hans Bethe, completing his doctorate at 24. While impressive, a PhD and postdoc position are standard academic career steps rather than material independent milestones. His Nobel-winning work on topological phase transitions came in the 1970s, well after age 26.
